content: Anise, also known as aniseed or less commonly as anís (with stress on the second syllable), is a flowering plant scientifically classified as Pimpinella anisum. It belongs to the family Apiaceae and is native to the eastern Mediterranean region and parts of Southwest Asia. This herbaceous annual plant typically grows to a height of about 1 meter. The leaves at the base of the plant are simple, measuring 2–5 cm in length, and are shallowly lobed. In contrast, the leaves higher up on the stems are feathery and pinnate, divided into numerous small leaflets. The plant produces small white flowers, approximately 3 mm in diameter, which are arranged in dense umbrella-shaped clusters called umbels. Its fruit is an oblong, dry schizocarp, measuring 3–5 mm in length. Certain species of Pimpinella serve as food sources for the larvae of some Lepidoptera species, such as the lime-speck pug and wormwood pug moths. Culinary Uses Anise is known for its sweet and highly aromatic properties, containing components that impart a licorice-like flavor. Aniseed is used in the production of British confectionery such as aniseed balls and traditional New Zealand sweets like aniseed wheels. It is a key ingredient in the Mexican drink atole, specifically in a variation called champurrado, which is similar to hot chocolate. Anise oil is utilized in Italian baking, particularly in making pizzelles (a type of cookie) and in the frosting of yellow Italian cake-like cookies known as Drops or Anise Drops. In Norway, anise flavoring is used in candies such as Knott, produced by Nidar. Anise toast, a type of dry bread, is popular in Italy. In India, anise (referred to as saunf or badi-sheb) is commonly consumed as a digestive aid after meals. Medicinal Uses The leaves of the anise plant are traditionally used to address digestive issues and to alleviate toothache. Its essential oil is also employed in the treatment of lice and scabies. In aromatherapy, aniseed essential oil is used to manage symptoms of colds and flu. It is currently being researched for its potential role in treating bird flu. In India, aniseed is also used as a natural mouth freshener and as a flavoring agent in certain foods. In the Middle East, aniseed is a key ingredient in the production of alcoholic beverages such as arak (Morocco) and ouzo (Greece). In Thailand, anise is used to flavor tea. Other Uses Anise can be processed into a liquid scent and is used in hunting and fishing. Its aroma, which resembles that of licorice, is applied to fishing lures to attract fish. The primary component of anise oil, anethole, serves as a precursor in the synthesis of certain psychedelic drugs, including 2C-B, 2C-I, and DOB. Anise is also the dominant flavor in absinthe and is used as a flavoring agent in various liqueurs such as pastis, ouzo, pernod, sambuca, raki, Becherovka, anice tutone, and Chartreuse. Interestingly, anise has a unique effect on some dogs, similar to the effect of catnip on cats. Some cats are also attracted to anise. It is safe for both cats and dogs to ingest in moderation, though excessive consumption should be avoided.
